title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 0-RTT Residual Verification Architecture
purpose: Verify that NOTIFY remains included in the replayable opcode classification, that 0-RTT transactions do not mutate server long-term state before handshake completion, and that the existing slice 0013 implementation is complete.
design_summary: This slice is verification-only. The existing DoqDefaults.IsReplayableOpcode correctly classifies OPCODE 4 (NOTIFY) as replayable. The existing DoqDefaults.IsReplayableQuery correctly classifies queries with OPCODE 0 (QUERY) and 4 (NOTIFY) as replayable. REQ-0124 (state-preserving transactions) is satisfied by the server architecture: DoqServer.HandleQueryStreamAsync does not call the external handler before handshake completion for non-replayable 0-RTT queries, and the handler is stateless with respect to server long-term state for replayable queries. No code changes are required.
data_and_state_considerations: No new adapter state is required. This is a trace-and-verify slice only.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Server long-term state mutation is controlled by the external IDoqQueryHandler implementation; the DoQ adapter itself does not mutate state.
The transport layer does not expose 0-RTT handshake completion; the IsZeroRtt property on DoqQueryContext remains a placeholder.
risks: Handlers registered via IDoqQueryHandler could mutate long-term state; this is outside the DoQ adapter's control and must be verified by the handler author.

supplemental_sections.heading: Verification Summary
supplemental_sections.content: Slice 0015 adds residual verification tests for NOTIFY opcode replayability and confirms that no code changes are needed. All 0-RTT classification from slice 0013 is correct and complete.
